## Agreement with the Manly-Jones algorithm

```{r}
analysis2_agreement |>
  dplyr::filter(
    classification_2 == "Manly-Jones algorithm",
    classification_1 %in% c("Core algorithm", "PMM")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    classification_1 = classification_1,
    n = c(
      "Core algorithm" = analysis2_n_compare[["core_algorithm"]],
      "PMM" = analysis2_n_compare[["pmm"]]
    )[classification_1]
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(classification_1, n, three_class_kappa, binary_kappa) |>
  gt::gt(rowname_col = "classification_1") |>
  gt::tab_stubhead("Compared with Manly-Jones algorithm") |>
  gt::cols_label(
    n = "N",
    three_class_kappa = "Normal, MCI, Dementia (weighted kappa)",
    binary_kappa = "Dementia vs. no dementia (kappa)"
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_integer(columns = n) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(three_class_kappa, binary_kappa), decimals = 2) |>
  gt::opt_stylize(6, color = "gray") |>
  gt::tab_options(
    table.width = gt::pct(90),
    table.font.size = gt::px(26),
    column_labels.font.size = gt::px(22),
    stub.font.size = gt::px(24),
    data_row.padding = gt::px(6)
  )
```

<div style="font-size: 0.5em; line-height: 1.2;">
HRS/HCAP 2016 participants. Kappa measures agreement beyond chance (0 = chance, 1 = perfect). The three-class kappa uses quadratic weights, so a Normal vs. MCI disagreement counts less than a Normal vs. Dementia disagreement. All kappas use HCAP population weights (HCAP16WGTR). Both the core algorithm and the PMM are calibrated and scored in the same sample, so their agreement is an in-sample estimate.
</div>
